subject: Complete incremental index lifecycle
description:
## What to build

Complete the semantic index lifecycle so synchronization performs content-hash-correct incremental updates, recovers safely from failures, rejects incompatible state, and explicitly deletes derivative state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unchanged complete index returns already_current without loading or invoking the model.
- [ ] New files alone are embedded; changed files replace and re-embed all owned chunks atomically; deleted files and chunks are removed without unrelated embeddings.
- [ ] Completion snapshots are written only after the planned run succeeds, failed replacements are not accepted, and later synchronization can finish an incomplete index.
- [ ] Incompatible schema or compatibility fingerprints fail with explicit delete-then-index guidance and never rebuild implicitly.
- [ ] Synchronization and deletion share a vault-specific lock and release model, database, and lock resources through scoped finalizers.
- [ ] index --delete safely removes the database, sidecars, lock state, and derivative directory; returns deleted or already_absent; and preserves Markdown and shared model cache.
- [ ] Typed results, errors, and CLI tests cover all incremental counts and statuses.

subject: Preserve existing Git-ignore rules
description:
## Defect

The existing-vault repair uses `line.trim()` to recognize the semantic-index pattern and `existing.trimEnd()` to rebuild the file. It can mistake a leading-space pattern for the required entry and can corrupt unrelated escaped trailing-space patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Recognize only a Git-ignore rule that actually ignores `.agentic-memory/index/`.
- [ ] Preserve all pre-existing `.gitignore` bytes and rule semantics while appending the required entry, except for the minimum separator needed.
- [ ] Repeated repair remains idempotent.
- [ ] Add behavior tests using `git check-ignore` for leading-space and escaped trailing-space cases.
context:
## Rejected Work Item

`wi_2147071d658f49f9af1de36393a5fd69`

## Review evidence

`VaultGitIgnore.ts:32` treats `" .agentic-memory/index/"` as present even though Git does not ignore the index path; review reproduced `git check-ignore` exit 1. Lines 36-39 apply `trimEnd()`, converting a valid escaped-space rule such as `foo\ ` into `foo\`, changing existing Git behavior.

## Files and constraints

- `packages/core/src/vault/VaultGitIgnore.ts`
- `packages/core/test/model-provisioning.test.ts` or focused Git-ignore tests
- Existing vault Git and overwrite behavior must remain intact.
- Keep one owning module for Git-ignore repair semantics.

## Verification expectations

- Test a leading-space near-match, create `.agentic-memory/index/recall.db`, and require `git check-ignore` success after repair.
- Test an escaped trailing-space rule before/after repair and require both byte preservation and `git check-ignore` success.
- Test repeat idempotency.
- Run focused tests and `bun run check`.

subject: Respect Markdown fences in chunking
description:
## Defect

The semantic Markdown parser treats any line beginning with three backticks or tildes as a fence toggle without tracking the opening marker or its length. A valid four-backtick fence containing a three-backtick code sample therefore closes early, and a following `#` line inside the code block becomes a document heading. The ATX-heading matcher also strips an unspaced trailing hash, so `# C#` becomes heading path `C` even though the hash is content. Both cases corrupt heading paths, section boundaries, and formatted embedding prompts.

## Rejected Work Item

`wi_4d5393b52d4145eb91a535e98f17e913`

## Acceptance criteria

- Track the active fenced-code delimiter character and opening length so only a compatible closing fence ends the block.
- Keep headings inside valid backtick and tilde fences in chunk text and never promote them into heading paths, including longer outer fences containing shorter fence examples.
- Preserve unspaced trailing hash characters in ATX heading content while continuing to remove valid whitespace-separated closing hash sequences.
- Add deterministic regressions for a four-backtick fence containing triple backticks, a tilde-fence equivalent, and headings such as `# C#` versus `# C #`.

subject: Recognize indented ATX headings

subject: Preserve recall source exclusion
description:
## Defect

Deterministic recall now reads and validates every managed source document before applying `includeSources: false`. Excluded source files can therefore make ordinary recall fail or incur source I/O even though the prior public behavior filtered sources before reading them.

## Acceptance criteria

- Allow neutral managed-memory discovery to apply caller eligibility after normalization/classification but before symlink resolution, file reads, and hashing.
- Make deterministic recall with `includeSources: false` perform no source-file validation or I/O and preserve prior behavior.
- Keep semantic indexing on the select-all path so sources remain indexed and unsafe source symlinks remain rejected there.
- Add public recall regressions proving an excluded unsafe source does not fail ordinary recall while `includeSources: true` and indexing still reject it.
- Preserve one vault-owned managed-path classification contract.

subject: Encode libSQL database file URLs
description:
## Defect

The native libSQL repository builds its URL by concatenating `file:` with the absolute database path. Valid vault path characters such as `?`, `#`, and `%` are interpreted as URI syntax or invalid percent encoding, so indexing fails or targets the wrong path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Convert the absolute database path to a correctly encoded file URL using the platform/runtime URL API accepted by `@libsql/client`.
- Index vaults whose path contains URI-reserved filename characters at the exact intended `.agentic-memory/index/recall.db` path.
- Add real libSQL integration coverage for representative reserved characters, including `?`, `#`, and `%` where supported by the test platform.
- Preserve scoped client closure, typed repository errors, and current CLI contracts.
